events.verdict: McDaniels (MIN) moves alongside VanVleet's (TOR) path and maintains a legal guarding position as he contests the driving shot attempt.
Barnes (TOR) jumps slightly forward while contesting Anderson's (MIN) shot attempt and incidental contact occurs as both players are landing.
VanVleet (TOR) slightly extends his arms into Russell (MIN) as the pick is being set, and marginal contact occurs as he releases away.
Reid (MIN) initiates more than marginal contact to Barnes' (TOR) head while contesting the dunk.
VanVleet (TOR) and Anderson (MIN) mutually engage in the lane.

events.category: Turnover: Out of Bounds - Bad Pass Turn
events.verdict: The pass thrown by Russell (MIN) is last touched by Anderson (MIN) before going out of bounds.
VanVleet (TOR) briefly grasps McDaniels' (MIN) arm as both players come together as the screen is set.
VanVleet (TOR) turns as Russell (MIN) moves through the lane and marginal contact occurs between the two players.
Barnes (TOR) initiates contact to Russell's (MIN) front that affects his SQBR.
VanVleet (TOR) places his hands on Russell (MIN) and engages, but releases without affecting his FOM.

VanVleet's (TOR) arm is extended towards Russell (MIN) and he initiates contact with Russell's arm as he rips through. The contact occurs during the side-to-side motion by Russell and is considered a non-shooting foul.

events.category: Turnover: Lost Ball Out of Bounds
events.verdict: Replay review of the OOB called on Barnes (TOR) pursuant to a coach's challenge was deemed unsuccessful as Barnes was confirmed to be the last to touch the ball. For clarification, before TOR called a timeout to challenge the out-of-bounds call, referees conducted a replay review because they were reasonably certain that the game clock expired due to a clock malfunction, and the game clock was reset to 00:00.4 (the out of bounds situation was not a reviewable matter under this trigger). MIN was awarded possession and called a timeout to advance the ball. Upon being notified of MIN's possession, TOR called a timeout and unsuccessfully challenged the out of bounds. [This comment was changed from the original post, which incorrectly stated that the review of the clock malfunction occurred during the MIN timeout, when in fact it was conducted before the MIN timeout.]
